notes: Finkelstein 1990a covers the 1987 sounding at Dhahr Mirzbaneh, not Kh. Samiyye. The text puts that spur north of Kh. Samiya, and the publication's map ref 18180/15595 is exactly S1644's point (181800/155950), so features of the excavated site take grid S1644. Grid identifications: (1) s4_f2 to s4_f5: S1647 records 'hundreds of shaft tombs in several concentrations', notes 'previously excavated by Lapp' and cites this publication, so it matches the four spur cemeteries (nos. 1-4; Lapp's A, B and C among them). (2) s4_f7: the 1970 tombs 'near Kh. Samiya' are cemetery no. 6 (the same excavators in n. 7-8 and n. 29). One of them held the 'Ein Samiya silver cup, which E222/S1676 list ('Ein Samiya cemetery, same point). (3) s4_f9: S1683, a shaft-tomb cemetery of c. 40 tombs that cites this publication, near el-Qasr (S1684). No grid used: cemetery 5 (it may be S1671, but that is not clear) and cemetery 7 (c. 60 tombs, which may be S1666/E219, but those points disagree with each other and with Fig. 1). They take words positions relative to the spur or the wadi. Fig. 1 (p. 239) has a 0-500 m scale but no north arrow, and Figs. 4, 5 and 7 do not show the unit's point, so no plan positions are used. Not coded: the tumulus (only 'perhaps' a tomb, a bamah or a cult centre); cupmarks; the 'Ein Samiya spring (a spring, with no pool described); Lyon's 'cemetery near 'Ein Samiya' (the same as nos. 5-6). No pool and no non-tomb pit appear in the publication.
